extracted.intended_audience: readers of early-20th-century literary fiction / magazine readers
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpts of short fiction / magazine stories (early 20th-century) used as examples of narrative craft and atmosphere. The page contains two fiction pieces and incidental authorial commentary about storytelling qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of causation and climax
rubrics_metrics.description: "the two presented the most complete possible unity of causation and climax."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as an explicit storytelling virtue: linked events should build logically toward a single, coherent climax; this unity is described as making the pair of incidents 'admirable' as a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of mood / atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: "They were enveloped, too, in the consistency of mood loosely called atmosphere; that is, all the details of their surrounding combined to color the attentive mind with morbid shadows."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atmosphere should be sustained across details — setting, sensory notes, and incidental specifics — so that the cumulative effect colors the reader's emotional response (here, toward 'morbid shadows'). Use concrete, surrounding details to maintain a consistent mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verisimilitude via manner and concrete detail
rubrics_metrics.description: "She was not capable of invention, he pointed out, and continued that no one could make up details such as that, finally, of the Rock of Ages. The irony was too biting and inevitable. Her manner alone put what she related beyond dispute."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character credibility and the specificity of small, particular details (props, gestures, mannerisms) can persuade readers of a narrative's truthfulness; a convincing manner and concrete particulars lend authenticity even when claims are extraordinary.
